CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, skip this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) — highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** — override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** — lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you—follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `references/copilot-tools.md` (Copilot CLI), `references/codex-tools.md` (Codex) for tool equivalents. Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

```dot
digraph skill_flow {
    "User message received" [shape=doublecircle];
    "About to EnterPlanMode?" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Already brainstormed?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" [shape=box];
    "Might any skill apply?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke Skill tool" [shape=box];
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" [shape=box];
    "Has checklist?" [shape=diamond];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [shape=box];
    "Follow skill exactly" [shape=box];
    "Respond (including clarifications)" [shape=doublecircle];

    "About to EnterPlanMode?" -> "Already brainstormed?";
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Invoke brainstorming skill" [label="no"];
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Might any skill apply?" [label="yes"];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" -> "Might any skill apply?";

    "User message received" -> "Might any skill apply?";
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Invoke Skill tool" [label="yes, even 1%"];
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Respond (including clarifications)" [label="definitely not"];
    "Invoke Skill tool" -> "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'";
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";
    "Has checklist?" -> "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [label="yes"];
    "Has checklist?" -> "Follow skill exactly" [label="no"];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" -> "Follow skill exactly";
}
```

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills could apply, use this order:

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task
2. **Implementation skills second** (frontend-design, mcp-builder) - these guide execution

"Let's build X" → brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
"Fix this bug" → debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

The skill itself tells you which.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.

- Fetching and updating schemas

    ## Security Guidance: Secure-by-Default Libraries

    When writing code, consider using these security-focused libraries that follow secure-by-default principles:

    ### Key Security Libraries by Category:

    **HTTP Security Headers**
    - Helmet.js (Node.js), secure_headers (Ruby) - Set protective HTTP response headers

    **XSS Prevention**
    - DOMPurify (JS), Bleach (Python), Ammonia (Rust) - Sanitize HTML safely

    **CSRF Protection**
    - Gorilla CSRF (Go), anti-csrf (PHP) - Token-based CSRF defense

    **Cryptography**
    - Google Tink (multi-language) - Secure, easy-to-use crypto APIs
    - Themis (14+ platforms) - High-level crypto framework

    **Input Validation**
    - Safe-regex - Detect catastrophic regex
    - defusedxml (Python) - Prevent XML attacks

    **SSRF Defense**
    - ssrf_filter (Ruby), ssrf-req-filter (Node.js) - Block private IP connections

    **Deserialization**
    - SerialKiller (Java) - Safe deserialization

    **Template Engines**
    - Mustache, Handlebars, Liquid - Logic-less templates prevent injection

    For detailed information, see: https://github.com/tldrsec/awesome-secure-defaults

    💡 When implementing security features, prefer these well-tested libraries over custom solutions.

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 12, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2027, 1, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_none_due_at_anchors_on_now(self) -> None:
        result = compute_next_due_at(None, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result is not None
        # Should be roughly 1 day from now.
        delta = result - timezone.now()
        assert timedelta(hours=23) < delta < timedelta(hours=25)

    def test_dashboard_returns_all_lists_with_types_and_counts(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

        base_updated_at = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
        list_specs = [
            ("Groceries", "grocery", 2),
            ("Hardware", "hardware", 1),
            ("Pharmacy", "pharmacy", 3),
            ("General", "general", 0),
            ("Clothes", "clothes", 1),
            ("Weekend", "grocery", 4),
            ("Projects", "hardware", 2),
            ("Errands", "general", 1),
        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(
                family=family,

            for item_index in range(item_count):
                GroceryItem.objects.create(
                    grocery_list=grocery_list,

                    created_by=user,

                    "list_type": list_type,
                    "item_count": item_count,

@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_create_tasks_from_capture_reloads_locked_capture_before_creating_tasks() -> (
    None
):
    api_test = TestOrganizeApi()
    family, user = api_test._setup_family()
    existing_task = create_task_from_household_action(
        family=family,
        title="Existing task",
        created_by=user,
        source_client_app="organize",
    )
    capture = InboxCapture.objects.create(
        family=family,
        created_by=user,
        capture_type=InboxCapture.CaptureType.PHOTO,
        status=InboxCapture.Status.NEEDS_REVIEW,
        normalized_payload={
            "suggested_tasks": [{"title": "Existing task", "notes": ""}]
        },
    )
    stale_capture = InboxCapture.objects.get(pk=capture.pk)

    capture.status = InboxCapture.Status.CONVERTED
    capture.converted_task = existing_task
    capture.normalized_payload = {"created_task_ids": [str(existing_task.id)]}
    capture.save(
        update_fields=["status", "converted_task", "normalized_payload", "updated_at"]
    )

    returned_tasks = create_tasks_from_capture(
        stale_capture,
        reviewed_tasks=[{"title": "New duplicate task", "notes": "", "selected": True}],
    )

    assert [task.id for task in returned_tasks] == [existing_task.id]
    assert FamilyTask.objects.filter(source_object_id=str(capture.id)).count() == 0

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 12, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2027, 1, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_none_due_at_anchors_on_now(self) -> None:
        result = compute_next_due_at(None, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result is not None
        # Should be roughly 1 day from now.
        delta = result - timezone.now()
        assert timedelta(hours=23) < delta < timedelta(hours=25)


@pytest.mark.django_db
class TestRecurrenceSpawn:
    def _setup_family(self) -> Any:
        family = FamilyGroup.objects.create(name="Recurrence Family")
        user = User.objects.create_user(username="rec-user", password="pass")
        FamilyMembership.objects.create(
            user=user, family=family, role="PARENT", is_admin=True
        )
        profile = user.profile
        profile.primary_family = family
        profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
        family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
        family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
        return family, user

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_returns_none_for_non_recurring(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="One-off",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE,
        )
        assert spawn_next_occurrence(task) is None
        assert FamilyTask.objects.filter(family=family).count() == 1

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_inherits_fields_and_sets_parent(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        original_due = timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Water plants",
            notes="Use the watering can",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=original_due,
            assigned_to=user,
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY,
        )
        spawned = spawn_next_occurrence(task)
        assert spawned is not None
        assert spawned.title == "Water plants"
        assert spawned.notes == "Use the watering can"
        assert spawned.status == FamilyTask.Status.PENDING
        assert spawned.assigned_to_id == user.id
        assert spawned.recurrence == FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY
        assert spawned.recurrence_parent_id == task.id
        assert spawned.due_at == original_due + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_spawn_preserves_series_root_for_grandchild(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        root = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Trash",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY,
        )
        child = spawn_next_occurrence(root)
        assert child is not None
        grandchild = spawn_next_occurrence(child)
        assert grandchild is not None
        # Grandchild's parent should still point at the root, not the child.
        assert grandchild.recurrence_parent_id == root.id


@pytest.mark.django_db
class TestFamilyTaskListFilters:
    def _setup_family(self) -> Any:

        user = User.objects.create_user(username="filter-user", password="pass")
        FamilyMembership.objects.create(

        )

        profile.save(update_fields=["primary_family"])
        family.feature_settings.organize_enabled = True
        family.feature_settings.save(update_fields=["organize_enabled", "updated_at"])
        return family, user

    def _make_client(self, user: Any) -> Any:
        client = APIClient()
        client.force_authenticate(user=user)
        return client

    def test_list_hides_completed_by_default(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Active 1",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            created_by=user,
        )
        FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Done 1",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.COMPLETED,
            created_by=user,
        )
        response = self._make_client(user).get(
            "/api/organize/tasks/", HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize"
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        titles = [task["title"] for task in response.data]
        assert titles == ["Active 1"]

    def test_list_include_completed_caps_at_twenty(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        for i in range(25):
            FamilyTask.objects.create(
                family=family,
                title=f"Done {i}",
                status=FamilyTask.Status.COMPLETED,
                completed_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=i),
                created_by=user,
            )
        FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Active",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            created_by=user,
        )
        response = self._make_client(user).get(
            "/api/organize/tasks/?include_completed=true",
            HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize",
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        titles = [task["title"] for task in response.data]
        assert "Active" in titles
        completed_titles = [t for t in titles if t.startswith("Done")]
        assert len(completed_titles) == 20
        # Most recent (lowest index) should be present; oldest should be excluded.
        assert "Done 0" in completed_titles
        assert "Done 24" not in completed_titles

    def test_list_assignee_me_filter(self) -> None:

    def test_completing_recurring_task_via_api_spawns_next(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        due = timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Water plants",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=due,
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY,
        )
        response = self._make_client(user).patch(
            f"/api/organize/tasks/{task.id}/",
            {"status": "COMPLETED"},
            format="json",
            HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize",
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        # Original is completed; a new PENDING occurrence was created.
        occurrences = FamilyTask.objects.filter(
            family=family, title="Water plants"
        ).order_by("due_at")
        assert occurrences.count() == 2
        first_task = occurrences.first()
        assert first_task is not None
        assert first_task.id == task.id
        next_task = occurrences.last()
        assert next_task is not None
        assert next_task.id != task.id
        assert next_task.status == FamilyTask.Status.PENDING
        assert next_task.recurrence == FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY
        assert next_task.recurrence_parent_id == task.id
        assert next_task.due_at == due + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_completing_non_recurring_task_does_not_spawn(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Solo",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE,
        )
        response = self._make_client(user).patch(
            f"/api/organize/tasks/{task.id}/",
            {"status": "COMPLETED"},
            format="json",
            HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize",
        )

        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:

    def test_dashboard_returns_all_lists_with_types_and_counts(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()

        client.force_authenticate(user=user)

        base_updated_at = timezone.now() - timedelta(hours=1)
        list_specs = [
            ("Groceries", "grocery", 2),
            ("Hardware", "hardware", 1),
            ("Pharmacy", "pharmacy", 3),
            ("General", "general", 0),
            ("Clothes", "clothes", 1),
            ("Weekend", "grocery", 4),
            ("Projects", "hardware", 2),
            ("Errands", "general", 1),
        ]

        expected_lists: list[dict[str, str | int]] = []
        for index, (name, list_type, item_count) in enumerate(list_specs, start=1):
            grocery_list = GroceryList.objects.create(
                family=family,
                owner=user,
                name=name,
                list_type=list_type,
            )
            GroceryList.objects.filter(pk=grocery_list.pk).update(
                updated_at=base_updated_at + timedelta(minutes=index)
            )
            grocery_list.refresh_from_db(fields=["updated_at"])

            for item_index in range(item_count):
                GroceryItem.objects.create(
                    grocery_list=grocery_list,
                    name=f"{name} item {item_index + 1}",
                    created_by=user,
                )

            expected_lists.insert(
                0,
                {
                    "id": str(grocery_list.id),
                    "name": name,
                    "list_type": list_type,
                    "item_count": item_count,
                },
            )

        response = client.get("/api/organize/dashboard/", HTTP_X_CLIENT_APP="organize")

        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.data["grocery_lists"] == response.data["lists"]
        assert [
            {
                "id": item["id"],
                "name": item["name"],
                "list_type": item["list_type"],
                "item_count": item["item_count"],
            }

class TestComputeNextDueAt:
    def test_none_returns_none(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.now()
        assert compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE) is None

    def test_daily_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))  # Sunday
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_weekly_advances_seven_days(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY)
        assert result == anchor + timedelta(days=7)

    def test_weekdays_friday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        friday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 20, 9, 0))
        assert friday.weekday() == 4
        result = compute_next_due_at(friday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sat, which rolls to Mon (+3 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == friday + timedelta(days=3)

    def test_weekdays_saturday_skips_to_monday(self) -> None:
        saturday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 21, 9, 0))
        assert saturday.weekday() == 5
        result = compute_next_due_at(saturday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        # +1 day is Sun, which rolls to Mon (+2 days total).
        assert result is not None
        assert result.weekday() == 0
        assert result == saturday + timedelta(days=2)

    def test_weekdays_midweek_advances_one_day(self) -> None:
        wednesday = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 18, 9, 0))
        assert wednesday.weekday() == 2
        result = compute_next_due_at(wednesday, FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKDAYS)
        assert result == wednesday + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_monthly_simple(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 3, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 4, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2026 is not a leap year -> Feb 28.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 2, 28, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_clamps_jan31_to_february_leap_year(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 1, 31, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        # 2028 is a leap year -> Feb 29.
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2028, 2, 29, 9, 0))

    def test_monthly_december_rolls_to_january(self) -> None:
        anchor = timezone.make_aware(datetime(2026, 12, 15, 9, 0))
        result = compute_next_due_at(anchor, FamilyTask.Recurrence.MONTHLY)
        assert result == timezone.make_aware(datetime(2027, 1, 15, 9, 0))

    def test_none_due_at_anchors_on_now(self) -> None:
        result = compute_next_due_at(None, FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY)
        assert result is not None
        # Should be roughly 1 day from now.
        delta = result - timezone.now()
        assert timedelta(hours=23) < delta < timedelta(hours=25)

        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="One-off",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.NONE,
        )

        assert FamilyTask.objects.filter(family=family).count() == 1

    def test_spawn_next_occurrence_inherits_fields_and_sets_parent(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        original_due = timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)
        task = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Water plants",
            notes="Use the watering can",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=original_due,
            assigned_to=user,
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY,
        )

        assert spawned is not None
        assert spawned.title == "Water plants"
        assert spawned.notes == "Use the watering can"
        assert spawned.status == FamilyTask.Status.PENDING
        assert spawned.assigned_to_id == user.id
        assert spawned.recurrence == FamilyTask.Recurrence.DAILY
        assert spawned.recurrence_parent_id == task.id
        assert spawned.due_at == original_due + timedelta(days=1)

    def test_spawn_preserves_series_root_for_grandchild(self) -> None:
        family, user = self._setup_family()
        root = FamilyTask.objects.create(
            family=family,
            title="Trash",
            status=FamilyTask.Status.PENDING,
            due_at=timezone.now(),
            created_by=user,
            recurrence=FamilyTask.Recurrence.WEEKLY,
        )
        child = spawn_next_occurrence(root)
        assert child is not None
        grandchild = spawn_next_occurrence(child)
        assert grandchild is not None
        # Grandchild's parent should still point at the root, not the child.
        assert grandchild.recurrence_parent_id == root.id
